title: Introducing: Analyze Data on Lists and Queries (2023 release wave 2)

chapters.title: Context: changing world of analytics and reporting
Vision for analytics and reporting in Business Central
Feature overview: analyze data on lists and queries
Demo: analyzing data on customer ledger entries
Query objects and inventory analysis demo
Analytical content vision for business central
Click-once installers and data analysis persistence
Analytical requirements, reporting strategy, and AL queries

features.name: Analyze data on list pages
features.description: Enables self-service data analysis directly in the Business Central client on list pages. Users can quickly extract insights, design analysis with different tabs, apply grouping, filters, and save analysis for later use.
caveats: Data size limitation of 100,000 rows removed in this release
Feature can be turned off by developer or permission settings

features.name: Share data analysis
features.description: Users can share their data analysis definitions with coworkers and friends after saving them.

features.name: Analysis menu persistence
features.description: The state of analysis menus (open or closed) and analysis mode choice are now persisted per list page, making features easier to discover.

features.name: Remove data size limitation
features.description: In 2023 release Wave 2, the 100,000 row data size limitation on analyze data mode was completely removed, allowing users to analyze as much data as desired.
caveats: Large datasets may take longer to load

features.name: Analyze data on query objects
features.description: Extends data analysis capability to query objects, not just list pages. Query objects can now be used as the data foundation for ad hoc analysis and reporting with the same analysis UI as lists.

features.name: Query objects as data foundation for analysis
features.description: Queries can now be used as the data foundation for ad hoc analysis with the same analysis UI. Users can join queries with related tables to create rich analysis scenarios.

features.name: Analysis on queries with same UI as lists
features.description: Analysis on queries now comes with the same analysis UI as data analysis on lists, providing a consistent user experience.

features.name: Query documentation with teaching tips and links
features.description: Developers can add teaching tips and specific documentation links to queries to help users find and understand queries more easily.

features.name: Join related table data in queries
features.description: Queries can join related table data to provide more meaningful information in analysis, such as location names instead of location codes.

features.name: Queries in report and role explorer
features.description: Queries are now searchable in Tell Me and show up in role explorer and report explorer as other UI elements, making them more discoverable.
caveats: Some features came in late and are likely available in version 23.1

features.name: Report and role explorer for content discoverability
features.description: New role explorer and report explorer concepts make reporting content more discoverable in business central, addressing feedback that business central comes with many hidden reports.

features.name: Built-in analytical content vision
features.description: Vision to build in analytical content for every use case or main feature in business central, with queries and reports being added to fulfill this.

features.name: Share analysis definitions with coworkers
features.description: Users can share analysis definitions with coworkers through links that can be placed in teams, web pages, or other locations. The shared link creates a copy of the analysis for the recipient.
caveats: Shared definitions are independent copies, not live-linked

features.name: Company-specific and company-agnostic analysis links
features.description: When sharing analysis definitions, users can choose whether the link is for a specific company or works across all companies.

features.name: Click-once installers for analysis
features.description: Pre-built click-once scenarios allow users to create analysis definitions with a single click, with example scenarios covering finance, sales, inventory and compliance.

features.name: Data analysis persistence of UI state
features.description: Business central persists the user's menu choices in data analysis, remembering which analysis tabs were used previously.

features.name: Data analysis execute permission
features.description: New system permission called Data analysis execute controls whether users can perform data analysis. Users with this permission can analyze on objects they have permission for.

features.name: Sample click-once scenarios repository
features.description: Open source repository at aka.ms/bc data analysis containing 15 different sample scenarios showing how to use data analysis and click-ones across finance, sales, inventory and compliance.

features.name: AL Queries for analytics
features.description: AL queries are being invested in as a powerful tool for data measurement and analysis, moving beyond just performance tuning. Instead of building reports, developers can build queries to support analytical needs.
caveats: requires learning shift from report-building mindset

features.name: Data sets for Excel layouts
features.description: Data sets are being promoted for Excel layouts as an alternative to traditional report building, allowing developers to create data sets that can be consumed by Excel.

features.name: Ad hoc analysis on list pages
features.description: Adding existing table fields to optimize PE allows for ad hoc analysis directly on list pages, providing a way to support analytical needs without building formal reports.
